rows.original_prompt: Bump the version in `recall/version.py` from 0.9.7 to 0.9.8. Do it with a re-runnable script at `scripts/bump_version.py` that takes the new version as its argument, because CI will call it on every release, and run it now so the change is applied. Leave the working tree otherwise untouched.

items.text:
⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

Context: the bump was needed because master sat **155 commits past `v0.7.0`** with the version never
moved, and the editable installs meant every tree ran new code while reporting 0.7.0 — which
mislabels mem-bench submissions, since they pass the version as `--system-version`.

The user's shorthand for these is memory, code and doc. `memory`'s pipeline fingerprint is
`77c918cd93f9200b36e505ae874d49a1949f04a8a85ce5b8b72a8c135b472db7` and is unchanged across all
four of its generations, so a rebuild would reuse every unmoved file rather than re-embed.

Row counts for `memory`: **46,190 in `recall_chunks_v1`** and **9,687 in `chunks`** (dormant, the
pre-production corpus). Both exist. Counting only the second is the trap below.

🔁 **Corrected 2026-08-25: 46,190 is NOT the live corpus, it is the table total across all six
generations, and the live one is 9,608.** `recall_chunks_v1` is keyed by `generation_id` and
retains retired and ready generations, by design, so a bare `count(*)` over the table is 4.8x the
corpus any query can actually reach:

| state | corpus_version | chunks |
|---|---|---:|
| retired | memory-2026-08-17 | 8,671 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-20 | 9,053 |
| ready | memory-2026-08-22-voyage | 9,411 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 9,444 |
| failed | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 3 |
| **active** | **memory-20260824-voyage-r3** | **9,608** |

🔑 Note the shape of this one: the fix for "the check counted the wrong table" (`chunks`, 9,687)
was to count the right table — and 9,687 and 9,608 are within 1% of each other, so the corrected
check produced a number that *looked* like confirmation while being a different quantity entirely.
**Group by generation, or the total silently answers a question nobody asked.**

## ⚠️ `doc` is serving bge-large, not voyage-4

- **`bin/build_generation.sh`** hardcoded `fastembed:BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5` and was dated
  2026-08-17. Running it against this corpus would have built a wrong-model generation in silence.
  It now refuses with an explanation; override is `BUILD_GENERATION_I_KNOW_IT_IS_STALE=1`, and the
  original is `bin/build_generation.sh.pre-voyage.bak`.
- **`bin/index_memory.sh`** line 156 counted `chunks` alone and printed "corpus: 9687 chunks" while
  the live corpus held 46,190. It now prints `RECALL_ENV`, both tables and the active generation.
  Original at `bin/index_memory.sh.pre-generations.bak`.

**PR [#221](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/221) MERGED** as `6e1a736`, 2026-08-06.
Detail lives in `docs/ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` on master; this is the pointer plus what is not
in there.

## The result

**No context mode alters the raw chunk content or the raw content hashes it stores.** Three
independent comparisons against `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, over the corpus and glob the promotion
campaign used: **746 sources, 21,924 chunks per generation, 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 hash mismatches**,
equal chunk counts, on all three. Archived at
`/var/lib/recall-benchmarks/2026-08-06-context-mode-generation-parity/`, 8 of 8 files verify.

Measured 2026-08-22 on VPS2's `recall_repos`:

```sql
SELECT left(source,3), count(*) FROM chunks WHERE tenant_id='memory' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
--  C:\   9449
--  /ho      5
```

**Why this matters the moment embedding moves to VPS2** ([[embedding-runs-on-vps2-one-at-a-time]]).
`source` is the row key `replace_sources` DELETEs by and the key `source_content_hashes()` compares
against, so a corpus embedded under one path and re-indexed under another does not update: it
writes a second copy of every chunk, every file looks unseen and is re-embedded, and every search
that finds one of those memos returns it twice. This is not a prediction. The mirror image of it
was measured the same day in the other direction: **452 duplicate rows in `recall` and 615 in

## 🔁 Re-measured 2026-08-22: it is now 34 to 55 minutes, and the SPREAD is the finding

Three full runs on this workstation in one day, same commit range, session container up:

| run | result | wall |
|---|---|---|
| plugin branch | 6486 passed, 34 skipped | **34:33** |
| release-script branch | 6503 passed, 34 skipped | **54:30** |
| earlier, 2 failures | 6423 passed, 2 failed, 34 skipped | 36:28 |

📊 **Statistical filtering ported to CODE 2026-07-24** — `~/.claude/tools/cca_scorecard.py`
(+ `test_cca_scorecard.py`, 11 tests). Step 2.6 now RUNS it (`--json`) instead of describing the
arithmetic in prose: a statistic eyeballed from a JSONL file is not a measurement, and the `n<10` guard
is exactly the rule that silently stops being applied when a model does the arithmetic in its head.
🔑 **Additive-only is STRUCTURAL, not promised**: `Report` has no field able to express a
drop/suppress/exclude/demote, pinned by `test_never_emits_a_drop` — so "a suppression rate is not a
score" cannot regress into the code later as an optimisation. Also surfaces `rows_malformed` rather
than silently skipping bad rows (a corrupted ledger must not render identically to a clean one).

- **The script's log lied by omission**: printed `upserted 14 day(s)` while filtering the zeros out of its own display (`if earn > 0 or n > 0`). All good news; 6 silent destructive writes per run. *A summary that only prints non-zero rows cannot show you a zeroing bug.*
- **The monitor worked perfectly and was ignored**: `lrp-reward-monitor` raised a `gap` breach for **every zeroed day, every day, for ~3 weeks** (`pm_reward_monitor_alerts`). It read as noise. The detector was never the weak link — the response was. Those same alerts later became the independent evidence that repaired the data.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

Found 2026-07-25 during the RE-call security audit: master had been red at `602f006` (the 0.6.0
release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

Context: the bump was needed because master sat **155 commits past `v0.7.0`** with the version never
moved, and the editable installs meant every tree ran new code while reporting 0.7.0 — which
mislabels mem-bench submissions, since they pass the version as `--system-version`.
Related: [[incident-fsck-repairs-metadata-not-file-contents-pyc-2026-08-02]] ·
[[lane_recall_2026-07]] · [[lane_membench_2026-08]].

**2. ⛔ Do NOT run `uv lock` on Windows to bump this repo's version.** On Windows/CPython 3.14 it
resolved a **28-line** diff that rewrote platform markers on the CUDA/nvidia packages, dropping
`sys_platform == 'linux'` from `nvidia-cublas`, `nvidia-cuda-nvrtc`, `cuda-pathfinder` and others.
CI resolves on **Linux**. Committing it would have changed dependency resolution for every consumer
in order to fix a version string. **Edit the `recall-rag` block's own `version =` line surgically**
(1-line diff) and confirm with `uv lock --check` (rc 0). The CI audit job accepts this.

🔑 **`uv lock --check` returning 0 on YOUR platform is not evidence the lockfile is right for CI's.**

## ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-02 — `recall-rag 0.8.0` is live on PyPI

## Packaging facts (correct these — they changed)
- **PyPI package name is `recall-rag`** (import stays `recall`). NOT `re-call` — the earlier memo's
  "`re-call` name is free / wheel `re_call-0.5.0`" is superseded; the project actually shipped as
  `recall-rag`. Single-version-source guard: `test_smoke.py` asserts `recall.__version__` ==
  pyproject version; a bump must touch `recall/__init__.py` AND `pyproject.toml` AND `uv.lock`

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

Found 2026-07-25 during the RE-call security audit: master had been red at `602f006` (the 0.6.0
release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

`77c918cd93f9200b36e505ae874d49a1949f04a8a85ce5b8b72a8c135b472db7` and is unchanged across all
four of its generations, so a rebuild would reuse every unmoved file rather than re-embed.

Row counts for `memory`: **46,190 in `recall_chunks_v1`** and **9,687 in `chunks`** (dormant, the
pre-production corpus). Both exist. Counting only the second is the trap below.

🔁 **Corrected 2026-08-25: 46,190 is NOT the live corpus, it is the table total across all six
generations, and the live one is 9,608.** `recall_chunks_v1` is keyed by `generation_id` and
retains retired and ready generations, by design, so a bare `count(*)` over the table is 4.8x the
corpus any query can actually reach:

| state | corpus_version | chunks |
|---|---|---:|

  original is `bin/build_generation.sh.pre-voyage.bak`.

  the live corpus held 46,190. It now prints `RECALL_ENV`, both tables and the active generation.

```sql
SELECT left(source,3), count(*) FROM chunks WHERE tenant_id='memory' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
--  C:\   9449
--  /ho      5
```

that finds one of those memos returns it twice. This is not a prediction. The mirror image of it
was measured the same day in the other direction: **452 duplicate rows in `recall` and 615 in

memory pipeline. The right fix is a flock on the
  docs side; the memory side can only narrow the window.

  generations for a 1,286-file corpus. Putting the rebuild on a schedule turns that into
  unbounded growth. Tracked separately.

The user's shorthand for these is memory, code and doc. `memory`'s pipeline fingerprint is
`77c918cd93f9200b36e505ae874d49a1949f04a8a85ce5b8b72a8c135b472db7` and is unchanged across all
four of its generations, so a rebuild would reuse every unmoved file rather than re-embed.

Row counts for `memory`: **46,190 in `recall_chunks_v1`** and **9,687 in `chunks`** (dormant, the
pre-production corpus). Both exist. Counting only the second is the trap below.

🔁 **Corrected 2026-08-25: 46,190 is NOT the live corpus, it is the table total across all six
generations, and the live one is 9,608.** `recall_chunks_v1` is keyed by `generation_id` and
retains retired and ready generations, by design, so a bare `count(*)` over the table is 4.8x the
corpus any query can actually reach:

| state | corpus_version | chunks |
|---|---|---:|
| retired | memory-2026-08-17 | 8,671 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-20 | 9,053 |
| ready | memory-2026-08-22-voyage | 9,411 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 9,444 |
| failed | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 3 |
| **active** | **memory-20260824-voyage-r3** | **9,608** |

🔑 Note the shape of this one: the fix for "the check counted the wrong table" (`chunks`, 9,687)
was to count the right table — and 9,687 and 9,608 are within 1% of each other, so the corrected
check produced a number that *looked* like confirmation while being a different quantity entirely.
**Group by generation, or the total silently answers a question nobody asked.**

  2026-08-17. Running it against this corpus would have built a wrong-model generation in silence.
  It now refuses with an explanation; override is `BUILD_GENERATION_I_KNOW_IT_IS_STALE=1`, and the
  original is `bin/build_generation.sh.pre-voyage.bak`.
- **`bin/index_memory.sh`** line 156 counted `chunks` alone and printed "corpus: 9687 chunks" while
  the live corpus held 46,190. It now prints `RECALL_ENV`, both tables and the active generation.
  Original at `bin/index_memory.sh.pre-generations.bak`.

**PR [#221](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/221) MERGED** as `6e1a736`, 2026-08-06.
Detail lives in `docs/ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` on master; this is the pointer plus what is not
in there.

**No context mode alters the raw chunk content or the raw content hashes it stores.** Three
independent comparisons against `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, over the corpus and glob the promotion
campaign used: **746 sources, 21,924 chunks per generation, 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 hash mismatches**,
equal chunk counts, on all three. Archived at
`/var/lib/recall-benchmarks/2026-08-06-context-mode-generation-parity/`, 8 of 8 files verify.

Measured 2026-08-22 on VPS2's `recall_repos`:

```sql
SELECT left(source,3), count(*) FROM chunks WHERE tenant_id='memory' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
--  C:\   9449
--  /ho      5
```

`source` is the row key `replace_sources` DELETEs by and the key `source_content_hashes()` compares
against, so a corpus embedded under one path and re-indexed under another does not update: it
writes a second copy of every chunk, every file looks unseen and is re-embedded, and every search
that finds one of those memos returns it twice. This is not a prediction. The mirror image of it
was measured the same day in the other direction: **452 duplicate rows in `recall` and 615 in

memory pipeline. The right fix is a flock on the
  docs side; the memory side can only narrow the window.
- **Nothing retires old generations**: `recall_chunks_v1` held 143,985 rows across ~14
  generations for a 1,286-file corpus. Putting the rebuild on a schedule turns that into
  unbounded growth. Tracked separately.

Related: [[embedding-runs-on-vps2-one-at-a-time]], [[vps2-memory-refresh-is-the-generation-chain]],

re-deriving the body with `parse_frontmatter` and re-chunking with a candidate configuration
reproduces the stored chunk list exactly when the candidate is right. Measured over the `memory`
corpus, 1,058 usable sources: `chunk_text(max_chars=800, overlap=80)` reproduced **1,058 of 1,058**,

pass**, so this is exhaustive rather than sampled.

Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX
(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(".py") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so
`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with
the non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.

def`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than

Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX
(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(".py") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so
`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with

⚠️ `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async

`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a

any chunker change, not an exotic case.** It follows directly from the omission above: the run after
the change skips every unchanged file, so those keep their old chunking while newly changed files
get the new one. Anything that must assert one `ChunkerIdentity` for a whole corpus (a generation's

deliberate chunking sweep.

items.text:
⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

Found 2026-07-25 during the RE-call security audit: master had been red at `602f006` (the 0.6.0
release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

Context: the bump was needed because master sat **155 commits past `v0.7.0`** with the version never
moved, and the editable installs meant every tree ran new code while reporting 0.7.0 — which
mislabels mem-bench submissions, since they pass the version as `--system-version`.
Related: [[incident-fsck-repairs-metadata-not-file-contents-pyc-2026-08-02]] ·
[[lane_recall_2026-07]] · [[lane_membench_2026-08]].

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

(CVE-2026-69247). PR #183 bumped it to 50.0.0 and merged to `master`. Re-running #182's `audit`

🔑 **A zero from a search is a claim, and on this machine it is the claim most likely to be an
artefact.** Before reporting "this string appears nowhere", re-run the search a second way that
cannot be mangled. A false zero reads exactly like a clean result, and it argues for alarm rather
than against it, which is the direction that wastes other people's attention.

The same conversion hits `docker run -v /x:/y`, `ssh host "/path"`, `curl -d @/file` and any tool
taking a `/`-prefixed non-path argument, including regexes and `find -path`. `tar -cf C:/...`
fails the mirror-image way: it reads a Windows path as `host:file` and tries to resolve a remote
host, which is how the same session lost a first attempt at reproducing an artifact.

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

Two things the 0.9.0 release (2026-08-04) surfaced. Both are about the gap between *what the
version says* and *what actually runs*.

**2. ⛔ Do NOT run `uv lock` on Windows to bump this repo's version.** On Windows/CPython 3.14 it
resolved a **28-line** diff that rewrote platform markers on the CUDA/nvidia packages, dropping
`sys_platform == 'linux'` from `nvidia-cublas`, `nvidia-cuda-nvrtc`, `cuda-pathfinder` and others.
CI resolves on **Linux**. Committing it would have changed dependency resolution for every consumer
in order to fix a version string. **Edit the `recall-rag` block's own `version =` line surgically**
(1-line diff) and confirm with `uv lock --check` (rc 0). The CI audit job accepts this.

🔑 **`uv lock --check` returning 0 on YOUR platform is not evidence the lockfile is right for CI's.**

## ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-02 — `recall-rag 0.8.0` is live on PyPI

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

Found 2026-07-25 during the RE-call security audit: master had been red at `602f006` (the 0.6.0
release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

## Bugs found while building it (both silent)
- **Denominator poisoning**: the index was written for every fix file even when a version failed to
  fetch. `bartfeenstra/betty#4027` ("Add missing `__init__.py` files") had **zero auditable files** —
  a fix that CREATES a file has no buggy version — and would have scored as a MISS on a file no
  auditor was ever shown. Biases recall DOWNWARD = the flattering direction for a contamination
  critique, which is why it mattered. Now: index only if both versions fetched; bugs with none
  excluded LOUDLY → `harness/fresh_exclusions.json`.
- **Workflow `args` arrives as a JSON STRING, not an array** → `pipeline()` threw in 95ms.
  Script now normalises and **throws with a count** if empty — otherwise it would "succeed" having
  probed nothing.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

Found 2026-07-25 during the RE-call security audit: master had been red at `602f006` (the 0.6.0
release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

**2. ⛔ Do NOT run `uv lock` on Windows to bump this repo's version.** On Windows/CPython 3.14 it
resolved a **28-line** diff that rewrote platform markers on the CUDA/nvidia packages, dropping
`sys_platform == 'linux'` from `nvidia-cublas`, `nvidia-cuda-nvrtc`, `cuda-pathfinder` and others.
CI resolves on **Linux**. Committing it would have changed dependency resolution for every consumer
in order to fix a version string. **Edit the `recall-rag` block's own `version =` line surgically**
(1-line diff) and confirm with `uv lock --check` (rc 0). The CI audit job accepts this.

🔑 **`uv lock --check` returning 0 on YOUR platform is not evidence the lockfile is right for CI's.**

## ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-02 — `recall-rag 0.8.0` is live on PyPI

Context: the bump was needed because master sat **155 commits past `v0.7.0`** with the version never
moved, and the editable installs meant every tree ran new code while reporting 0.7.0 — which
mislabels mem-bench submissions, since they pass the version as `--system-version`.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

🔑 **The version appears in at least five places and a release that misses one is broken:**
`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

Launch assets live in `launch/terminal-video/`: a rendered 45s terminal demo (mp4, preview gif,
contact sheet, still), generated by `render_terminal_video.py` from `storyboard.md`.

**How to apply:** before cutting a release, grep the version string across the repo rather than
bumping `pyproject.toml` alone. Related: [[recall-repo-organization]],
[[commit-signing-squash-merge]].

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

⛔ **The publish is manual and that is why it rots.** `.github/workflows/publish-mcp.yml` is
`workflow_dispatch` only, so the registry sat at 0.9.5 from 2026-08-15 while 0.9.6, 0.9.7 and 0.9.8
shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

**Preflight before publishing**, because a registry entry IS the install command: confirm the pinned
version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

Related: [[a-probe-that-matches-its-own-command]].

When a release bumps `version` in `pyproject.toml` without regenerating `uv.lock`, the lock still
pins the OLD project version. `uv lock --check` then fails, and in RE-call's CI that step **gates
the `audit` job** — so `pip-audit` never reaches the dependency set. Dependency CVE scanning stops
running on every PR, and the failure reads as "the lockfile step is broken", not "the security
control is absent".

Found 2026-07-25 during the RE-call security audit: master had been red at `602f006` (the 0.6.0
release) with the CVE gate unrunnable ever since. Fixed in [PR #87](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/87);
`pip-audit` then ran clean (0 CVEs). One line — only the project's own version moved.

## Packaging facts (correct these — they changed)
- **PyPI package name is `recall-rag`** (import stays `recall`). NOT `re-call` — the earlier memo's
  "`re-call` name is free / wheel `re_call-0.5.0`" is superseded; the project actually shipped as
  `recall-rag`. Single-version-source guard: `test_smoke.py` asserts `recall.__version__` ==
  pyproject version; a bump must touch `recall/__init__.py` AND `pyproject.toml` AND `uv.lock`
  (audit job runs `uv lock --check`).
- **CI = `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**, 4 jobs: `test` (real pgvector service, `pip install -e .[dev]`,
  coverage `--cov-fail-under=70` over recall+recall_mcp), `typecheck` (`.[dev]` + mypy, strict), `floor`
  (`uv pip install --resolution lowest-direct -e .[dev,mcp]`, real pg), `audit` (`uv lock --check` +
  pip-audit over

**Cost, 2026-08-21, reviewing four Dependabot lockfile PRs (#409, #413, #414, #415).** The two-dot
diff showed all four changing `recall-rag` in `uv.lock` from `version = "0.9.6"` to `"0.9.5"`, on
the same line, in all four. I concluded they carried a hidden version regression *and* that they
mutually conflicted, and started planning four sequential merges with a Dependabot rebase between
each. Both conclusions were false. `c319a36b` (#419) had bumped the version to 0.9.6 on master
after Dependabot branched; not one of the four touched that line. Against their real merge base
the four hunks were **disjoint** (uv.lock lines 1817, 2943, 3577, 4522), they merged cleanly in
one pass, and `uv lock --check` plus `pip-audit` both passed on the combined result.

Two audit findings were MOOT on master and correctly dropped rather than "fixed": write-path
reconnect (master already routes writes through `_with_retry`) and the lockfile (PR #2 shipped
`uv.lock`). Still open by choice: store thread-safety/connection pool (MCP server is
single-writer today), source-scoped supersession ambiguity, per-file embed-and-persist,
concurrent batch dispatch, eval-set size.

⚙️ **uv.lock must be regenerated on LINUX** (`docker run ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm
uv lock`) — running it on Windows rewrites ~28 platform markers. CI's `audit` job runs
`uv lock --check` and will catch a stale project version after any bump.

Context: the bump was needed because master sat **155 commits past `v0.7.0`** with the version never
moved, and the editable installs meant every tree ran new code while reporting 0.7.0 — which
mislabels mem-bench submissions, since they pass the version as `--system-version`.

⚠️ Two consequences for the next release: the tag subject must **not** be prefixed with the version
(the workflow prepends `$GITHUB_REF_NAME — ` itself, so a prefixed subject would double it), and
expect to fix the title by hand afterwards until `release.yml` is repaired.

## Release ≠ bump
`.github/workflows/release.yml` **publishes to PyPI on tag push**. So bumping and releasing are
separable, and a version-bump PR must not carry a tag. Cutting the release is a deliberate,
separate act. Distribution name is **`recall-rag`**, never `recall` (a squatting package shares the
import name).

**Bumping RE-call's version touches FOUR files.** Missing any of them is caught by CI, but only
after a red run:

| file | guarded by |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` (`version = `) | `tests/test_smoke.py::test_version_matches_pyproject` |
| `recall/__init__.py` (`__version__`) | same test |
| **`CITATION.cff`** (`version: `) | `test_smoke.py::test_citation_version_matches_pyproject` |
| **`uv.lock`** (the `recall-rag` package block) | the CI **`audit`** job, `uv lock --check` |

Plus `CHANGELOG.md`: rename `## [Unreleased]` to `## [X.Y.Z] — DATE` (**em dash**, matching the
existing headings) and add a fresh empty `[Unreleased]`. `release.yml` extracts release notes with
`awk` keyed on `index($0, "## [" v "]") == 1`, so the heading format is load-bearing.

Context: the bump was needed because master sat **155 commits past `v0.7.0`** with the version never
moved, and the editable installs meant every tree ran new code while reporting 0.7.0 — which
mislabels mem-bench submissions, since they pass the version as `--system-version`.
Related: [[incident-fsck-repairs-metadata-not-file-contents-pyc-2026-08-02]] ·
[[lane_recall_2026-07]] · [[lane_membench_2026-08]].

`pyproject.toml`, `recall/__init__.py`, `uv.lock`, `CITATION.cff`, and `server.json` (twice: top
level `version` and the package `version`, plus inside the `--from` runtime argument string). Two
separate commits on 2026-08-10 existed only to repair version drift.

shipped. Anyone installing from the registry got a build three releases old. `scripts/release.py`
now prints a reminder at the end of a bump; adding `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` would close it
permanently and is an open decision, not an oversight.

version exists on PyPI and that every extra in the pin (`recall-rag[mcp,fastembed]==X.Y.Z`) is
declared on that exact version.

corpus any query can actually reach:

| state | corpus_version | chunks |
|---|---|---:|
| retired | memory-2026-08-17 | 8,671 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-20 | 9,053 |
| ready | memory-2026-08-22-voyage | 9,411 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 9,444 |
| failed | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 3 |
| **active** | **memory-20260824-voyage-r3** | **9,608** |

The user's shorthand for these is memory, code and doc. `memory`'s pipeline fingerprint is
`77c918cd93f9200b36e505ae874d49a1949f04a8a85ce5b8b72a8c135b472db7` and is unchanged across all
four of its generations, so a rebuild would reuse every unmoved file rather than re-embed.

Row counts for `memory`: **46,190 in `recall_chunks_v1`** and **9,687 in `chunks`** (dormant, the
pre-production corpus). Both exist. Counting only the second is the trap below.

🔁 **Corrected 2026-08-25: 46,190 is NOT the live corpus, it is the table total across all six
generations, and the live one is 9,608.** `recall_chunks_v1` is keyed by `generation_id` and
retains retired and ready generations, by design, so a bare `count(*)` over the table is 4.8x the
corpus any query can actually reach:

| state | corpus_version | chunks |
|---|---|---:|
| retired | memory-2026-08-17 | 8,671 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-20 | 9,053 |
| ready | memory-2026-08-22-voyage | 9,411 |
| retired | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 9,444 |
| failed | memory-2026-08-22-voyage-r2 | 3 |
| **active** | **memory-20260824-voyage-r3** | **9,608** |

🔑 Note the shape of this one: the fix for "the check counted the wrong table" (`chunks`, 9,687)
was to count the right table — and 9,687 and 9,608 are within 1% of each other, so the corrected
check produced a number that *looked* like confirmation while being a different quantity entirely.
**Group by generation, or the total silently answers a question nobody asked.**

## ⚠️ `doc` is serving bge-large, not voyage-4

- **`bin/build_generation.sh`** hardcoded `fastembed:BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5` and was dated
  2026-08-17. Running it against this corpus would have built a wrong-model generation in silence.
  It now refuses with an explanation; override is `BUILD_GENERATION_I_KNOW_IT_IS_STALE=1`, and the
  original is `bin/build_generation.sh.pre-voyage.bak`.
- **`bin/index_memory.sh`** line 156 counted `chunks` alone and printed "corpus: 9687 chunks" while
  the live corpus held 46,190. It now prints `RECALL_ENV`, both tables and the active generation.
  Original at `bin/index_memory.sh.pre-generations.bak`.

**PR [#221](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/221) MERGED** as `6e1a736`, 2026-08-06.
Detail lives in `docs/ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` on master; this is the pointer plus what is not
in there.

## The result

**No context mode alters the raw chunk content or the raw content hashes it stores.** Three
independent comparisons against `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, over the corpus and glob the promotion
campaign used: **746 sources, 21,924 chunks per generation, 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 hash mismatches**,
equal chunk counts, on all three. Archived at
`/var/lib/recall-benchmarks/2026-08-06-context-mode-generation-parity/`, 8 of 8 files verify.

Measured 2026-08-22 on VPS2's `recall_repos`:

```sql
SELECT left(source,3), count(*) FROM chunks WHERE tenant_id='memory' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
--  C:\   9449
--  /ho      5
```

**Why this matters the moment embedding moves to VPS2** ([[embedding-runs-on-vps2-one-at-a-time]]).
`source` is the row key `replace_sources` DELETEs by and the key `source_content_hashes()` compares
against, so a corpus embedded under one path and re-indexed under another does not update: it
writes a second copy of every chunk, every file looks unseen and is re-embedded, and every search
that finds one of those memos returns it twice. This is not a prediction. The mirror image of it
was measured the same day in the other direction: **452 duplicate rows in `recall` and 615 in

memory pipeline. The right fix is a flock on the
  docs side; the memory side can only narrow the window.
- **Nothing retires old generations**: `recall_chunks_v1` held 143,985 rows across ~14
  generations for a 1,286-file corpus. Putting the rebuild on a schedule turns that into
  unbounded growth. Tracked separately.

Related: [[embedding-runs-on-vps2-one-at-a-time]], [[vps2-memory-refresh-is-the-generation-chain]],
[[stop-proposing-to-rebuild-the-corpus]].

runs sync, rebuild, calibrate, promote and VERIFIES the corpus matches the active generation; scheduled task `recall-memory-refresh` fires it hourly, debounced to 6h on success, so an unclosed session no longer strands the corpus.
- [Generation gc is step 6 of the memory pipeline](generation-gc-is-step-6-of-the-memory-pipeline.md) — `recall generation gc` existed with zero callers while ~15 generations of chunk rows accumulated; since 2026-08-27 it runs after every promote (retention-days 2, retain-previous 2, best-effort, under embed.lock); READY generations need `abandon` first, and `--check` now prints the awaiting-gc count.
- [A script edited while running dies with a garbled syntax error](a-script-edited-while-running-dies-with-a-garbled-syntax-error.md) — bash reads scripts lazily,

Measured 2026-08-25 on VPS2 with the correct embedder: `recall.cli search` prints
`generation=legacy` and reads the legacy **`chunks`** table (9,687 rows for `memory`, last indexed
2026-08-24), while the server reads **`recall_chunks_v1`** at the certified active generation
(9,608 rows). **Two corpora, 0.8% apart in size, both plausible, both answering.** The CLI's
results are ungated: no generation binding, no certified threshold, no `trust_state` at all.

🔑 So "I tested it with the CLI" is not a test of what a session gets, and the sizes are close
enough that no sanity check on the result count will catch it. Use the CLI to look things up; use
the SERVER, or `scripts/session-corpus.sh status`, to make any claim about what is served.

## Why ssh stdio rather than a tunnel

⚠️ **Two red herrings that appear at the same time and are NOT this.**
`[DEGRADED:INDEX_NOT_READY]` and `generation=legacy` print on every memory query. Search works
anyway, as the 0.558 above shows. Do not chase them while debugging a cosine.

🔁 **Corrected 2026-08-22: I first wrote that the tenant has NO row in `recall_generations`. It
does.** `gen_c5c87c56c24048cb8b8e6296656150e5` is `active`, activated 2026-08-20. I had read a
`limit 3` sample across all tenants and memory simply was not in it. The real reason for the

the legacy `chunks` table (9,477 rows). The pipeline fingerprint

## The result

**No context mode alters the raw chunk content or the raw content hashes it stores.** Three
independent comparisons against `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, over the corpus and glob the promotion
campaign used: **746 sources, 21,924 chunks per generation, 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 hash mismatches**,
equal chunk counts, on all three. Archived at
`/var/lib/recall-benchmarks/2026-08-06-context-mode-generation-parity/`, 8 of 8 files verify.

- **Always `--pool-size 4`** for backfill and launch runs. Direct connection mode loses the local
  Postgres connection during sparse backfill, because cursor reads and sparse writes share one held
  connection.
- **Never run the full SPLADE arm on local Windows CPU.** About 20 minutes for 1,227 chunks, so a
  500K-document corpus needs a rented GPU and a backgrounded launch.
- **Indexing progress is invisible to SQL while the process runs.** External counts returned zero
  even as the log printed `index wrote ...`. Trust `tail -f` on the run log, not a `SELECT count(*)`.
- **Throughput reference:** roughly 1,000 to 1,125 chunks/minute on both boxes, so full dense
  indexing is a 9 to 10 hour job before GPU SPLADE backfill even starts. Budget accordingly.
- `k=8` matched `k=10+` on

- **Background anything that indexes or embeds from the start** (`run_in_background`), rather than
  running it foreground and re-running after a timeout. The tool cannot be given more than 600 s.
- **Before calibrating, count generations**, not just chunks:
  `select generation_id, count(*) from recall_chunks_v1 group by 1;`
  One row is expected. Two rows with equal counts is this bug.
- **After any timeout, check for the effect before re-running the cause.** Here that was one query.
  The general form: a killed wrapper is not a rolled-back operation.

Discarding a stranded generation is a direct delete of its rows from `recall_chunks_v1` and
`recall_generations`; there is no CLI verb for abandoning one that is mid-lifecycle.

The visible symptom was three spurious nags in one session, each claiming "no readable summary
line" about a run whose output plainly said `141 passed`. I first explained it as the parser not
reading piped output. **That was wrong**, and wrong in the comfortable direction: it blamed my
invocation and implied nothing needed fixing. The real fault was two lines further down.

The expensive half is what the empty counts disable. `describe()` returns early on
`if not counts:`, so everything below it is unreachable:

- the `It was NOT green` warning, so a **failing** `-q` run reported only "no verdict";
- the `SKIP_ALARM`, whose own comment calls several hundred skips "the documented false-green
  signature in this repo", meaning the DB tests never ran.

The Bash tool caps at 600 s and silently clamps a larger `timeout` argument down to it. When a
`recall generation build` hit that cap I read the failure as "the build did not happen" and re-ran
it in the background.

Both runs completed. `recall_chunks_v1` then held **660 chunks for a 61-file corpus**: two
generations, 330 chunks each, the same documents twice.

🔑 **The fix is an invariant, not a habit.** Added as I7: resolve `recall.__file__` and refuse to
run when it is outside the repo root, recording the resolved path in the artifact's provenance
either way. Run as `python -m benchmarks.x` from the repo root (puts the root on `sys.path[0]` on
every platform) or with `PYTHONPATH=<repo>`. Note the guard as written is still too loose: it
accepts any `recall` nested ANYWHERE under the repo root, including an in-repo
`.venv/Lib/site-packages/recall`. Full context:
[[project-semantic-cache-fpr-measured-not-published-2026-08-04]].

✅ **Fixed 2026-08-22, and the fix is a different variable name, so this memo stays.** `recall`
now reads **`RECALL_INDEX_BATCH_CHUNKS`** in `Indexer.__init__` (host-wide, so a caller that never
heard of it is still bounded) and exposes `recall index --batch-chunks` per run. An explicit
argument beats the environment; a malformed value is ignored and logged rather than clamped.
`RECALL_FASTEMBED_BATCH` is still read nowhere and always will be: do not export it.

The batch is now one of three bounds rather than the only one, because it asks politely and a
cgroup does not. See [[embedding-runs-on-vps2-one-at-a-time]] for the other two and for where the
embedding runs at all now.

Counting processes with `grep -F 'python -m recall_mcp.server'` on VPS2 reported **89**. The real
number was about **44**. Every server appeared twice: once as itself, and once as the ssh session
wrapper whose `--cmd=cd ... exec .venv/bin/python -m recall_mcp.server` contains the identical
string. The memory total was barely affected (wrappers are ~22 MB against ~815 MB), which is
exactly why nobody noticed: the alarming number was right and the count beside it was not.

**Why:** a launcher's command line CONTAINS the command it launches. Any pattern specific enough to
name the process is, by construction, also present in whatever spawned it: `ssh host '<cmd>'`,
`bash -c '<cmd>'`, `systemd-run ... <cmd>`, a supervisor, a container runtime.

**The chunker is not in it.** So a file whose bytes have not changed is skipped even when the
chunker that would now read it is a different one. Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does
**not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports "N unchanged" and
leaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.

To actually rebuild, change one of the three terms (a different embedder, a different context
policy) or delete the affected sources first and let the next run re-read them.

The source docstring calls widening the tuple out as a migration rather than a comment change,
because it re-fingerprints every indexed corpus at once. That is a real cost and the reason it has
not been done, not an oversight.

## Why ssh stdio rather than a tunnel

**Method lessons.** (1) *Two arms scoring byte-identically is a smell* — a control arm at
`--pool 100` scoring identically to `--pool 50` on all four k is what exposed the cap; the same
rule applied in reverse (a code-fix rerun NOT matching the DB-level run) exposed the multiplier.
(2) An offline replay that must reproduce published numbers before any analysis is trusted caught
a scoring divergence (dedupe-to-pages before vs after truncating to 20 chunks). (3) A DB test
fixture must `ANALYZE`: without statistics the planner picks an exact Sort plan and the test
passes for the wrong reason.

Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX
(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(".py") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so
`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with
the non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.

⚠️ `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async
def`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than
`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a
chunker that parses the language being added.

**Sorting a random sample and then stopping early is not sampling. It is taking the head.**

The shape, which looks harmless in review:

```python
for i in sorted(rng.sample(range(len(items)), pool_size)):
    if len(kept) == target:      # or: if too_big: break
        break
    kept.append(i)
```

The sort is usually added for a good reason (stable output order, corpus order in a prompt). The
early stop is usually added for a good reason (a target count, a size budget). **Together they mean
only the lowest-indexed part of the sample is ever considered**, and the more you oversample the
worse it gets, because the tail moves further out of reach.

🔁 **2026-08-15: violated three times in one session, and the second and third came AFTER I had
named this rule out loud.** `\\t` and `\\r` became a literal tab and CR inside a test file;
backticks in a `python -c` became command substitution; `\xef\xbb\xbf` and `\n` became a decoded

RE-call's evidence prompt wrapped a `json.dumps` payload in `<evidence_data>` … `</evidence_data>`
and handed it to a generator. `json.dumps` escapes `"`, `\` and control characters. It does **not**
escape `<` or `>`, and the delimiter is built from exactly those two characters.

A memory whose text, file name or chunk id contained `</evidence_data>` **closed the region early**,
and everything after it reached the model as free prose in its own instruction channel. Reproduced
by rendering one hit: the message contained two closing tags. `ensure_ascii=True` does not help —
it escapes non-ASCII, and `<` is ASCII.

**Delimiting without escaping the delimiter is not delimiting.**

| `mtrag-human/generation_tasks/RAG.jsonl` | 842 | identical shape |
| `scripts/evaluation/sample_data/responses-10.jsonl` | 10 | `answerability` **top-level, LOWER CASE** · `enrichments` **nested inside turns, 39 of them** |

hint about whether to abstain. It is easy to miss because attention goes to the label.

## Why this matters beyond pedantry

**How to apply:** when a session asks "where does X live / who calls Y / what
pattern handles Z", run `--code-search` *before* grep. Grep still wins for
exact-string lookups (typos, error messages, identifiers you already know).

## Schema (`code_chunks`)
- `id BIGSERIAL`, `path TEXT`, `language TEXT` (`python|markdown|sql`),
  `chunk_idx INT`, `start_line INT`, `end_line INT`, `content TEXT`,
  `content_tsv tsvector` (BM25), `embedding vector(1024)`, `sha256 TEXT`,
  `mtime TIMESTAMPTZ`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ`.
- Unique key: `(path, sha256)` — content-addressed, idempotent reindex.
- HNSW index `code_chunks_embedding_hnsw` on `embedding` (cosine).

shape only. **So no existing non-markdown corpus can be attested**, and re extraction alone cannot
distinguish "the extractor changed" from "the file is wrong". Same shape as
[[embedding-profile-id-lies-for-unregistered-models]]: fixing a writer does not repair rows already
written.

🔑 **A corpus can hold chunks from SEVERAL chunker eras at once, and that is the NORMAL result of
any chunker change, not an exotic case.** It follows directly from the omission above: the run after
the change skips every unchanged file, so those keep their old chunking while newly changed files
get the new one. Anything that must assert one `ChunkerIdentity` for a whole corpus (a generation's
`PipelineIdentity` carries exactly one) therefore cannot assume homogeneity. Check per source.

(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(".py") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so

```python

swapped = list(chunks)
if len(swapped) > 1:            # <- never true: they pack into ONE chunk

Four short paragraphs pack into a single chunk at `max_chars=800`, so the branch never ran and a
`sorted(produced) == sorted(stored)` mutant survived a suite of 27 green tests. The test file's own
docstring claimed every check fails when its behaviour is removed.

**Sorting a random sample and then stopping early is not sampling. It is taking the head.**

The shape, which looks harmless in review:

```python
for i in sorted(rng.sample(range(len(items)), pool_size)):
    if len(kept) == target:      # or: if too_big: break
        break
    kept.append(i)
```

The sort is usually added for a good reason (stable output order, corpus order in a prompt). The
early stop is usually added for a good reason (a target count, a size budget). **Together they mean
only the lowest-indexed part of the sample is ever considered**, and the more you oversample the
worse it gets, because the tail moves further out of reach.

Measured twice on recall's own `docs/` (1815 chunks over 51 files):

**First run (bug)**: Parse 51% (151/294), match 77.5% on parsable. Output for ~143 chunks was filing-text continuation instead of JSON.

**Root cause**: user content ≈4000 tokens, `max_length=2048` truncated mid-prompt; chat-template assistant marker survived but model lost context (system prompt + part of filing). truncation_side="left" attempt also failed — model still emitted continuation.

**Fix**: bump `max_length=8192` (Qwen2.5 supports 32K, vast.ai 5090 has VRAM). No truncation actually happens on the test set (avg 5K tokens), prompt arrives intact.

Build awkward characters with `chr(0xDCFF)`, or bind them to a named constant in the target file
(`BOM = b"\xef\xbb\xbf"`), rather than writing the escape inline. Print `ascii(value)` at the top
of a probe so the input is visible in the output. Tests and source written through the editor are
fine; it is only the shell transport that mangles.

🔁 **2026-08-15: violated three times in one session, and the second and third came AFTER I had
named this rule out loud.** `\\t` and `\\r` became a literal tab and CR inside a test file;
backticks in a `python -c` became command substitution; `\xef\xbb\xbf` and `\n` became a decoded
BOM and a real line break, leaving a file that would not parse. Each cost a correction round.

RE-call's evidence prompt wrapped a `json.dumps` payload in `<evidence_data>` … `</evidence_data>`
and handed it to a generator. `json.dumps` escapes `"`, `\` and control characters. It does **not**
escape `<` or `>`, and the delimiter is built from exactly those two characters.

A memory whose text, file name or chunk id contained `</evidence_data>` **closed the region early**,
and everything after it reached the model as free prose in its own instruction channel. Reproduced
by rendering one hit: the message contained two closing tags. `ensure_ascii=True` does not help —
it escapes non-ASCII, and `<` is ASCII.

**Delimiting without escaping the delimiter is not delimiting.**

**How to apply:** when a session asks "where does X live / who calls Y / what
pattern handles Z", run `--code-search` *before* grep. Grep still wins for
exact-string lookups (typos, error messages, identifiers you already know).

## Schema (`code_chunks`)
- `id BIGSERIAL`, `path TEXT`, `language TEXT` (`python|markdown|sql`),
  `chunk_idx INT`, `start_line INT`, `end_line INT`, `content TEXT`,
  `content_tsv tsvector` (BM25), `embedding vector(1024)`, `sha256 TEXT`,
  `mtime TIMESTAMPTZ`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ`.
- Unique key: `(path, sha256)` — content-addressed, idempotent reindex.
- HNSW index `code_chunks_embedding_hnsw` on `embedding` (cosine).

### 2026-08-12 SPLADE GPU preparation update

**Sorting a random sample and then stopping early is not sampling. It is taking the head.**

The shape, which looks harmless in review:

```python
for i in sorted(rng.sample(range(len(items)), pool_size)):
    if len(kept) == target:      # or: if too_big: break
        break
    kept.append(i)
```

The sort is usually added for a good reason (stable output order, corpus order in a prompt). The
early stop is usually added for a good reason (a target count, a size budget). **Together they mean
only the lowest-indexed part of the sample is ever considered**, and the more you oversample the
worse it gets, because the tail moves further out of reach.

Measured twice on recall's own `docs/` (1815 chunks over 51 files):

| site | sorted + early stop | sampled + continue |
|---|---|---|
| `queryset.generate_offline` chunk sampling | **3 of 51 files** | 21 of 51 |
| `llm.generate_llm` prompt budget trim | **3 of 51 files** | 21 of 51 |

Identical numbers, identical cause, two separate commits days apart. The second one was written
*after* fixing the first and after documenting the lesson in a comment three files away.

**The fix is always the same:** iterate in sampled order, use `continue` rather than `break` so one
oversized item does not end the selection, and sort only the KEPT subset afterwards if presentation
order matters.

**Fix**: bump `max_length=8192` (Qwen2.5 supports 32K, vast.ai 5090 has VRAM). No truncation actually happens on the test set (avg 5K tokens), prompt arrives intact.

🔑 **Chunk size is the whole cost model.** The first full arm used the product default 800-character
chunks: about 8M chunks, roughly 60 hours, stopped. Sampling the official ZIP showed median document
length near 10K characters, so 12K chunking projects about 624K chunks. The Vast scripts now default
to `ENTERPRISE_RAG_CHUNK_CHARS=12000` / `_OVERLAP=200` / `_BATCH_CHUNKS=32`; override only for a
deliberate chunking sweep.

Observed 2026-08-23, TWICE in one session: an Edit to `recall/decision_ledger.py` meant to put
the six-character escape for U+0000 into a comment, and then the memo documenting that mistake
reproduced it in its own index line. Both times the tool-call JSON decoded the escape, so the
file received a literal NUL byte. Three symptoms,
none naming the cause: subsequent Edits failed with "string not found" though the text looked
identical, Read displayed empty backticks where the byte sat, and the module would have failed to
import (Python refuses source containing NUL) had it been executed before the repair.

**Why:** JSON interprets `\uXXXX` escapes in strings; a payload meant to SHOW an escape must not
spell it as one.

Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX
(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(".py") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so
`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with
the non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.

⚠️ `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async
def`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than
`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a
chunker that parses the language being added.
